title: ARXIASK: given ONLY the questions that discriminate the inverted frontier pair, can either format recover the true order? (1,196 calls)
question: The 302 pool questions where arx_0314 and iask_pro differ by the key (arx 179 : iask 123, rate 0.593); every match decidable by construction; both formats, same judge / reference / rubric / mechanics; plus a length-matched control; per format, the arx win rate tested against 0.5 by two-sided binomial; accuracy vs key; share of verdicts going to the longer answer; the same on length-matched questions.

criteria.value: pairwise 0.496 (p = 0.95); pointwise 0.561 (p = 0.060), closer to the true 0.593 but not significant
pairwise 0.612; pointwise 0.667; when the reference is right 0.788 / 0.856, when wrong 0.146 / 0.160 (below chance: the judge picks the model matching a wrong reference)

sentence_of_record: ARXIASK (2026-09-13, 1,196 calls): on the 302 questions where arx and iask differ by the key, pairwise gives arx 0.496 (p = 0.95, accuracy 0.612) and pointwise 0.561 (p = 0.060, accuracy 0.667); neither recovers the true 0.593; length is not the cause (length-matched 0.490 / 0.562); THE CAUSE: the reference scores 0.860 on the pool but 0.726 on these questions and the judge follows it (accuracy 0.788 / 0.856 when the reference is right, 0.146 / 0.160 when wrong). A reference-based arena's power to order two models is bounded by the reference's accuracy on the subset where they differ.

plain_description.what: Uses only the 302 questions where two top models (arx and iask) differ by the answer key, so that every match has a known winner. Both are judged in pairwise and pointwise format, plus a version matched for answer length (1,196 calls).
plain_description.why: Asks why the judged arena puts these two frontier models in the wrong order: is it answer length or something else?
plain_description.information: Shows whether a judge can recover the true order when given only the questions that matter, and what blocks it. Result: neither format recovered the true order. Length was not the cause. The cause was that the reference answer shown to the judge is much worse on these questions (0.73 correct, against 0.86 overall), and the judge follows it. A judge that relies on a reference cannot order two models better than the reference is accurate on the questions where they differ. This was measured on an older judged set that is now classed as history, not evidence.
